evidence: service_supervisor.py:66 adds --parent-pid.
attach_owner_process (:88-97) opens a SYNCHRONIZE handle on Windows and uses os.kill(pid, 0) on POSIX.
supervise() checks owner_process_alive() first on every 2 s loop pass and breaks (:408-410). The supervisor has no child processes of its own; the only spawn is a detached Chrome Popen.
An owned supervisor waits for a busy singleton while its owner is alive (:513-519). This avoids a respawn plus request_recovery every 5 s.
release_owner_process() runs on both exit paths.

My in-process Windows check: attach True / alive True, then after kill alive False. A dead PID whose handle is released attaches False. A dead PID whose handle a parent still holds attaches True, but alive is False, so supervise exits on its first pass.

start.ps1:196-213 -ServiceRun appends --parent-pid $PID to the supervisor (as the dev-watch already had). It starts both processes with Start-Process -PassThru and restarts whichever HasExited every $ServiceRestartSeconds, which covers a crashed supervisor.

The logon task action is powershell.exe -File start.ps1 -ServiceRun (:468-473), so $PID is the task process. Stop-UserLogonTask and Unregister-UserLogonTask (StartupManager.ps1:330-356) stop it. The supervisor then exits within about 2 s, and dev-watch within 3 s (dev-watch.mjs:77-86, taskkill /T on its watchers). The claim path in service.ts cycle(), pullAndProcessTasks: takePrefetchedHeadTasks, then base pullTasksAcrossTypes (rotatesPullTaskTypes=false keeps dictionary before word_translation), then noteFastSignals. The cycleInFlight guard replaces the old polling flag.
releaseUndispatchedTasks in finally releases claimed tasks that were not started, through the old client, before cycleInFlight clears. Base start waits on cycleInFlight.
prepareActivation catches pool errors, and enqueuePending catches its own errors, so neither turns into a registration retry.

K6: enqueuePending, pull, release and queueDiff all go through WorkerApiClient (the native-host signer). queueDiff hits /api/queue-center/queues/{queue}/diff (client.key), and isDiffQueue accepts every contract task type key, dictionary types included.

There is one Gemini AsyncMutex, the private generationMutex at gemini-image.ts:113. gemini-image-generate.ts no longer has its own mutex and uses geminiImageTool.runExclusive(). Moving the mutex into the tab owner avoids an import cycle, and the requirement is met: one shared mutex, no second implementation.
execute() status goes through statusExclusive (:124), and execute() start goes through startExclusive (:147). The popup listener uses the same two entry points.
startExclusive does a bounded 20 s acquire, releases on a throw or a failed start, and otherwise holds a job lease.
The job lease settles on done, failed or unknown status, or on expiry (the deadline plus 5 s). An uncollected job goes through cancel() before the release (settleJobLease, in a finally).
cancel() is called only under the mutex: from generateOnce inside runExclusive, and from settleJobLease while the lease is held.
A timed-out waiter frees a late grant at once (:371-381).
status() now treats a failed job as final (:288-292).

non_blocking: utils.ts:246 stores config.userManifestPath in the result's error field, so the registration summary at :257 prints '[X] Chrome: Failed - <manifest path>'. The real reason is logged earlier by registerUserHost. Fix: have registerUserHost return the error message, or print the path under its own label.

gemini-image.ts:35-36: TAB_BUSY_ERROR and JOB_ABANDONED_ERROR are English literals that now reach the popup error line (useGeminiImage.ts:66 and :87). They follow this file's existing English MCP-protocol error convention, so they are accepted for the tool. A follow-up should map the busy and abandoned states to _locales keys on the popup path.

Bing race: if updateConfig with a new apiUrl arrives while a start is still in flight, base repoint's this.start() joins the running startOperation (AsyncOperationController returns the in-flight promise). That startOnce then sees isRunning=false after super.start and returns, so the worker stays stopped until the next Start. The race is rare; a follow-up could queue the repoint after startOperation.

Bing now also runs the base queue-diff poll: 3 GETs per second per worker, even during an outage or cooldown. Only the prefetch is gated (runtime.ts:451-454). A follow-up could add a base hook that skips the diff poll while the worker is paused.
service_supervisor.py:73 windows_kernel32() rebuilds the WinDLL and its argtypes on every 2 s owner check. Caching it once would be cheaper. Nit.

start.ps1:198 `$SupervisorArguments += @(...)` appends to an array, not to a string. The repository uses the same pattern (ClaudeTeamCommon.ps1:688-695), so I accept it under the no-string-append rule.

Worst-case interactive start latency is the 20 s lock wait plus start()'s own tab-ready wait of up to 20 s, which can exceed the 30 s bridge timeout while the tab is busy. With an idle tab, latency is unchanged.
